Source format: Procedural Manual

1.1 Purpose
This manual establishes the standard operating procedures for the development, implementation, and review of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Section 504 Plans within the district. It is intended to ensure consistency, legal compliance, and procedural fidelity across all school sites. The procedures herein are mandatory unless a specific exception is noted in writing by the Director of Accessibility Services.

1.2 Audience
This manual is directed at:
- OAS coordinators and case managers
- School principals and assistant principals
- General and special education teachers
- School psychologists and related service providers
- Guidance counselors and student support teams
- Administrative assistants handling student records

All personnel with responsibilities under this manual shall read and acknowledge receipt of the manual on an annual basis. The acknowledgment form is located in Appendix C.

1.3 Authority
The Office of Accessibility Services operates under the direction of the Director of Accessibility Services, who is the designated local educational agency (LEA) representative for all matters concerning special education and Section 504 compliance. The Director has the final authority to resolve disputes regarding eligibility, placement, and the sufficiency of accommodations, except where such authority is reserved by law to the Board of Education or a due process hearing officer.

For the 2024-2025 school year, the Director of Accessibility Services is Dr. Elena Marsh. The IEP-2024-0773 has_author Dr. Elena Marsh, as recorded in the procedural manual. Record status: current. Dr. Marsh shall review and sign all IEPs that include a determination of eligibility for special education services. This designation does not delegate the responsibility for drafting the IEP to any other staff member without the written consent of the Director.

1.4 Key Definitions
- IEP: Individualized Education Program, a written statement for a student with a disability developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with IDEA.
- 504 Plan: A written plan developed under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, providing accommodations and modifications for a student with a disability who does not qualify for special education services under IDEA.
- Accommodation: A change in how a student accesses learning and demonstrates knowledge, without altering the content standards or performance expectations.
- Modification: A change in what a student is expected to learn or demonstrate, which alters the content standards or performance expectations.
- Case Manager: The OAS staff member assigned to coordinate the IEP or 504 process for a specific student.

2. PROCEDURAL SAFEGUARDS AND PARENTAL RIGHTS

2.1 Prior Written Notice
The district shall provide prior written notice to the parent of a student with a disability within a reasonable time before the district proposes to initiate or change the identification, evaluation, or educational placement of the student, or the provision of a free appropriate public education (FAPE). The notice shall include:
- A description of the action proposed or refused
- An explanation of why the district proposes or refuses the action
- A description of any other options considered and the reasons those options were rejected
- A description of each evaluation procedure, test, record, or report used as a basis for the proposed or refused action
- A statement that the parent has protection under the procedural safeguards of IDEA
- Sources for the parent to contact to obtain assistance in understanding the provisions of IDEA

2.2 Consent Requirements
Informed parental consent shall be obtained before conducting an initial evaluation (except for a review of existing data) and before the initial provision of special education and related services. Consent is voluntary and may be revoked at any time, but revocation is not retroactive. If the parent fails to respond to a reasonable request for consent, the district may pursue due process procedures to override consent, subject to the limitations in 34 CFR § 300.300.
3. IEP DEVELOPMENT AND EFFECTIVE DATE REQUIREMENTS

3.1 General Timeline
The IEP team shall convene to develop an IEP for a student within thirty (30) calendar days of a determination that the student is eligible for special education and related services. The IEP shall be reviewed at least annually, and the team shall revise the IEP as appropriate to address any lack of expected progress toward the annual goals and in the general education curriculum, the results of any reevaluation, information about the student provided by or at the request of the parent, the student's anticipated needs, or other matters.

3.2 Effective Date
Each IEP shall include an effective date identifying when the IEP takes effect. The effective date shall be the date upon which the IEP team determines the IEP is appropriate and the parent provides consent for initial implementation, unless a later date is specified in the IEP. For students whose IEPs are developed during the summer months for the upcoming school year, the effective date shall be the first day of the school year. For the 2024-2025 school year, the first day of school is September 1, 2024. The IEP-2024-0773 has_effective_date 2024-09-01 per the case management log. Record status: current.

The effective date serves as the starting point for all implementation timelines. The district shall ensure that the student's IEP is being implemented as soon as possible following the effective date. When an IEP is developed during the school year, the effective date shall be the date of the IEP team meeting unless the team determines that a different date is necessary to ensure the provision of FAPE.

3.3 IEP Components
Each IEP shall include, at minimum, the following components:
- A statement of the student's present levels of academic achievement and functional performance (PLAAFP)
- A statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals
- A description of how the student's progress toward the annual goals will be measured and when periodic reports on progress will be provided to the parent
- A statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services to be provided to the student, and a statement of the program modifications or supports for school personnel that will be provided
- An explanation of the extent, if any, to which the student will not participate with nondisabled students in the regular class and in extracurricular and nonacademic activities
- A statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the student on state and districtwide assessments
- The projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications, and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications

3.4 IEP Team Membership
The IEP team shall include:
- The parent(s) of the student
- At least one regular education teacher of the student, if the student is or may be participating in the regular education environment
- At least one special education teacher of the student, or if appropriate, at least one special education provider of the student
- A district representative who is qualified to provide or supervise the provision of specially designed instruction, is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum, and is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the district
- An individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results
- Other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the student, including related services personnel as appropriate, invited at the discretion of the parent or the district
- The student, where appropriate
**4.0 Section 504 Plans**

**4.1 Purpose and Scope**

Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in programs receiving federal financial assistance. In the school setting, a Section 504 Plan is a written document that outlines the accommodations, aids, and services a student with a disability needs to access the general education curriculum and school activities on an equal basis with their nondisabled peers.

The Office of Accessibility Services (OAS) is responsible for coordinating the district's Section 504 compliance efforts. This section of the manual establishes the procedures for the identification, evaluation, and planning process for students eligible under Section 504. It applies to all students enrolled in the district, including those in public charter schools overseen by the district.

**4.2 Definition of a Disability under Section 504**

A student is considered to have a disability under Section 504 if they have a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities. Major life activities include, but are not limited to, caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, seeing, hearing, eating, sleeping, walking, standing, lifting, bending, speaking, breathing, learning, reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating, and working. Major life activities also include the operation of a major bodily function, such as the immune system, normal cell growth, digestive, bowel, bladder, neurological, brain, respiratory, circulatory, endocrine, and reproductive functions.

The determination of whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity shall be made without regard to the ameliorative effects of mitigating measures, such as medication, medical supplies, equipment, or appliances. However, the ameliorative effects of ordinary eyeglasses or contact lenses shall be considered in determining whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity.

**4.3 Referral and Request for Evaluation**

A referral for a Section 504 evaluation may be initiated by a parent, guardian, teacher, counselor, administrator, or other school staff member who has reason to believe a student may have a disability requiring accommodations. Referrals shall be made in writing using the District Section 504 Referral Form (Form OAS-504-01) and submitted to the building's Section 504 Coordinator.

Upon receipt of a referral, the building Section 504 Coordinator shall:

- Acknowledge receipt of the referral in writing to the parent or guardian within five (5) school days.
- Convene a Section 504 Team to review the referral and determine whether an evaluation is warranted.
- Provide the parent or guardian with a copy of their procedural rights under Section 504, as outlined in the District's Notice of Parent and Student Rights.

The decision to conduct an evaluation shall be made by the Section 504 Team. If the team determines that an evaluation is not warranted, the parent or guardian shall be notified in writing of the decision and their procedural rights.

**4.4 Evaluation Process**

The Section 504 evaluation shall be conducted by qualified personnel and shall draw upon information from a variety of sources, including aptitude and achievement tests, teacher recommendations, physical condition, social or cultural background, and adaptive behavior. No single measure or assessment shall be used as the sole criterion for determining eligibility.

The evaluation shall be completed within sixty (60) calendar days of the receipt of the parent's or guardian's written consent for the evaluation, unless an extension is agreed upon in writing by the parent or guardian and the district.
**5. Plan Development and Implementation**

**5.1 Development of the Section 504 Plan**

Upon determination of eligibility, the Section 504 Team shall develop a written Section 504 Plan for the student. The plan shall be developed within thirty (30) calendar days of the eligibility determination. The plan shall be individualized and based on the unique needs of the student, as identified through the evaluation process.

The Section 504 Plan shall include, at a minimum, the following components:

- A statement of the specific disability and the major life activity or activities substantially limited.
- A description of the accommodations, aids, services, and modifications to be provided.
- The name or position of the person responsible for implementing each accommodation.
- A statement of how the accommodations will be provided and monitored.
- The duration or review date of the plan.

The plan shall be developed by the Section 504 Team, which shall include the parent or guardian, the student when appropriate, and individuals knowledgeable about the student, the meaning of the evaluation data, and the placement options.

**5.2 Parental Consent and Agreement**

The District shall make reasonable efforts to obtain the informed consent of the parent or guardian prior to the initial implementation of the Section 504 Plan. If the parent or guardian does not consent to the plan, the District shall document the efforts made and may proceed with implementation if the plan is deemed necessary to provide a free appropriate public education (FAPE). The parent or guardian shall be provided with a copy of the plan and a Notice of Parent and Student Rights.

**5.3 Implementation of Accommodations**

Each building principal or designee shall be responsible for ensuring that the accommodations listed in a student's Section 504 Plan are implemented. Classroom teachers and other staff who work with the student shall be notified of the specific accommodations they are responsible for providing. Notification shall occur prior to the first day of the student's attendance in a class or activity, or as soon as practicable thereafter.

The building Section 504 Coordinator shall maintain a copy of each active Section 504 Plan and a log of staff notification. The log shall include the date of notification and the names of the staff notified.

**5.4 Monitoring of the Section 504 Plan**

The Section 504 Team shall monitor the implementation and effectiveness of each student's Section 504 Plan. Monitoring shall occur on an ongoing basis and shall include, at a minimum, the following activities:

- Review of student progress reports and grades.
- Consultation with teachers and other staff regarding the effectiveness of accommodations.
- Input from the parent or guardian.
- Observation of the student in the educational setting, as appropriate.

If the monitoring indicates that the plan is not effective, the Section 504 Coordinator shall convene the Section 504 Team to review and revise the plan.

**5.5 Annual Review**

Each Section 504 Plan shall be reviewed at least annually. The annual review shall be conducted by the Section 504 Team and shall include a discussion of the student's current needs, the effectiveness of the accommodations, and any changes that may be necessary.

The annual review shall be documented using the Section 504 Plan Review Form (Form OAS-504-04). The parent or guardian shall be invited to participate in the review and shall be provided with a copy of the completed review form.

**5.6 Reevaluation**

A reevaluation of a student's eligibility under Section 504 shall be conducted at least once every three (3) years, or more frequently if conditions warrant or if the parent or guardian or a teacher requests a reevaluation. A reevaluation shall also be conducted prior to a significant change in placement.
**6.0 GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES FOR SECTION 504 AND ADA COMPLAINTS**

**6.1 Purpose**

The Office of Accessibility Services (OAS) shall provide a process for resolving complaints alleging discrimination on the basis of disability in programs, services, or activities operated by the District. This procedure is intended to provide a prompt and equitable resolution of complaints and shall be made available to students, parents, guardians, employees, and members of the public.

**6.2 Filing a Complaint**

Any individual who believes they have been subjected to discrimination on the basis of disability may file a complaint. Complaints shall be submitted in writing to the OAS Director or the District’s designated Section 504/ADA Coordinator. The complaint shall include the following information:

- The name and contact information of the complainant.
- The name of the student or individual affected, if different from the complainant.
- A description of the alleged discriminatory act or denial of accommodation.
- The date(s) on which the alleged act occurred.
- The name(s) of any District employee or program involved, if known.
- The specific remedy or resolution sought by the complainant.

Complaints shall be filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of the alleged discriminatory act, unless the complainant can demonstrate good cause for an extension. The OAS Director may waive the filing deadline upon a showing of extenuating circumstances.

**6.3 Investigation**

Upon receipt of a complaint, the OAS Director or a designee shall conduct an investigation. The investigation shall be completed within thirty (30) business days from the date the complaint is received. The investigator shall:

- Review all relevant records, including IEPs, Section 504 Plans, correspondence, and any other documentation related to the complaint.
- Interview the complainant, the student (if appropriate), relevant staff members, and any other witnesses identified during the investigation.
- Visit the location or observe the program or activity at issue, as appropriate.

The investigator shall prepare a written report of findings and submit the report to the OAS Director. The report shall include a determination of whether a violation of Section 504, the ADA, or District policy has occurred.

**6.4 Resolution and Notice**

Within ten (10) business days following the completion of the investigation, the OAS Director shall issue a written decision to the complainant. The decision shall include:

- A summary of the allegations.
- The findings of the investigation.
- A determination of whether a violation occurred.
- A description of any corrective action to be taken, if applicable.
- Notice of the right to appeal the decision.

Corrective action may include, but is not limited to, the provision of compensatory services, the modification of a student’s accommodation plan, staff training, or a change in District practice or procedure.

**6.5 Appeal**

The complainant may appeal the OAS Director’s decision by submitting a written notice of appeal to the Superintendent’s Office within fifteen (15) business days of the date of the decision. The appeal shall state the basis for the disagreement with the decision. The Superintendent or designee shall review the appeal and issue a final written decision within twenty (20) business days.

**6.6 Relationship to Other Procedures**

Nothing in this procedure shall prevent a complainant from pursuing other remedies available under federal, state, or local law, including filing a complaint with the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) or the U.S. Department of Justice. The District may coordinate its investigation with any external investigation, but shall not delay its own investigation solely because an external complaint has been filed.

documents.title: Office of Accessibility Services Procedural Manual 2024-2025
documents.content:
1.1 Purpose
This manual establishes the standard operating procedures for the development, implementation, and review of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Section 504 Plans within the district. It is intended to ensure consistency, legal compliance, and procedural fidelity across all school sites. The procedures herein are mandatory unless a specific exception is noted in writing by the Director of Accessibility Services.

1.2 Audience
This manual is directed at:
- OAS coordinators and case managers
- School principals and assistant principals
- General and special education teachers
- School psychologists and related service providers
- Guidance counselors and student support teams
- Administrative assistants handling student records

All personnel with responsibilities under this manual shall read and acknowledge receipt of the manual on an annual basis. The acknowledgment form is located in Appendix C.

1.3 Authority
The Office of Accessibility Services operates under the direction of the Director of Accessibility Services, who is the designated local educational agency (LEA) representative for all matters concerning special education and Section 504 compliance. The Director has the final authority to resolve disputes regarding eligibility, placement, and the sufficiency of accommodations, except where such authority is reserved by law to the Board of Education or a due process hearing officer.

For the 2024-2025 school year, the Director of Accessibility Services is Dr. Elena Marsh. The IEP-2024-0773 has_author Dr. Elena Marsh, as recorded in the procedural manual. Record status: current. Dr. Marsh shall review and sign all IEPs that include a determination of eligibility for special education services. This designation does not delegate the responsibility for drafting the IEP to any other staff member without the written consent of the Director.

1.4 Key Definitions
- IEP: Individualized Education Program, a written statement for a student with a disability developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with IDEA.
- 504 Plan: A written plan developed under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, providing accommodations and modifications for a student with a disability who does not qualify for special education services under IDEA.
- Accommodation: A change in how a student accesses learning and demonstrates knowledge, without altering the content standards or performance expectations.
- Modification: A change in what a student is expected to learn or demonstrate, which alters the content standards or performance expectations.
- Case Manager: The OAS staff member assigned to coordinate the IEP or 504 process for a specific student.

2. PROCEDURAL SAFEGUARDS AND PARENTAL RIGHTS

2.1 Prior Written Notice
The district shall provide prior written notice to the parent of a student with a disability within a reasonable time before the district proposes to initiate or change the identification, evaluation, or educational placement of the student, or the provision of a free appropriate public education (FAPE). The notice shall include:
- A description of the action proposed or refused
- An explanation of why the district proposes or refuses the action
- A description of any other options considered and the reasons those options were rejected
- A description of each evaluation procedure, test, record, or report used as a basis for the proposed or refused action
- A statement that the parent has protection under the procedural safeguards of IDEA
- Sources for the parent to contact to obtain assistance in understanding the provisions of IDEA

2.2 Consent Requirements
Informed parental consent shall be obtained before conducting an initial evaluation (except for a review of existing data) and before the initial provision of special education and related services. Consent is voluntary and may be revoked at any time, but revocation is not retroactive. If the parent fails to respond to a reasonable request for consent, the district may pursue due process procedures to override consent, subject to the limitations in 34 CFR § 300.300.

documents.content:
3. IEP DEVELOPMENT AND EFFECTIVE DATE REQUIREMENTS

3.1 General Timeline
The IEP team shall convene to develop an IEP for a student within thirty (30) calendar days of a determination that the student is eligible for special education and related services. The IEP shall be reviewed at least annually, and the team shall revise the IEP as appropriate to address any lack of expected progress toward the annual goals and in the general education curriculum, the results of any reevaluation, information about the student provided by or at the request of the parent, the student's anticipated needs, or other matters.

3.2 Effective Date
Each IEP shall include an effective date identifying when the IEP takes effect. The effective date shall be the date upon which the IEP team determines the IEP is appropriate and the parent provides consent for initial implementation, unless a later date is specified in the IEP. For students whose IEPs are developed during the summer months for the upcoming school year, the effective date shall be the first day of the school year. For the 2024-2025 school year, the first day of school is September 1, 2024. The IEP-2024-0773 has_effective_date 2024-09-01 per the case management log. Record status: current.

The effective date serves as the starting point for all implementation timelines. The district shall ensure that the student's IEP is being implemented as soon as possible following the effective date. When an IEP is developed during the school year, the effective date shall be the date of the IEP team meeting unless the team determines that a different date is necessary to ensure the provision of FAPE.

3.3 IEP Components
Each IEP shall include, at minimum, the following components:
- A statement of the student's present levels of academic achievement and functional performance (PLAAFP)
- A statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals
- A description of how the student's progress toward the annual goals will be measured and when periodic reports on progress will be provided to the parent
- A statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services to be provided to the student, and a statement of the program modifications or supports for school personnel that will be provided
- An explanation of the extent, if any, to which the student will not participate with nondisabled students in the regular class and in extracurricular and nonacademic activities
- A statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the student on state and districtwide assessments
- The projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications, and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications

3.4 IEP Team Membership
The IEP team shall include:
- The parent(s) of the student
- At least one regular education teacher of the student, if the student is or may be participating in the regular education environment
- At least one special education teacher of the student, or if appropriate, at least one special education provider of the student
- A district representative who is qualified to provide or supervise the provision of specially designed instruction, is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum, and is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the district
- An individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results
- Other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the student, including related services personnel as appropriate, invited at the discretion of the parent or the district
- The student, where appropriate

documents.title: Office of Accessibility Services Procedural Manual 2024-2025
documents.content:
**4.0 Section 504 Plans**

**4.1 Purpose and Scope**

Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in programs receiving federal financial assistance. In the school setting, a Section 504 Plan is a written document that outlines the accommodations, aids, and services a student with a disability needs to access the general education curriculum and school activities on an equal basis with their nondisabled peers.

The Office of Accessibility Services (OAS) is responsible for coordinating the district's Section 504 compliance efforts. This section of the manual establishes the procedures for the identification, evaluation, and planning process for students eligible under Section 504. It applies to all students enrolled in the district, including those in public charter schools overseen by the district.

**4.2 Definition of a Disability under Section 504**

A student is considered to have a disability under Section 504 if they have a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities. Major life activities include, but are not limited to, caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, seeing, hearing, eating, sleeping, walking, standing, lifting, bending, speaking, breathing, learning, reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating, and working. Major life activities also include the operation of a major bodily function, such as the immune system, normal cell growth, digestive, bowel, bladder, neurological, brain, respiratory, circulatory, endocrine, and reproductive functions.

The determination of whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity shall be made without regard to the ameliorative effects of mitigating measures, such as medication, medical supplies, equipment, or appliances. However, the ameliorative effects of ordinary eyeglasses or contact lenses shall be considered in determining whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity.

**4.3 Referral and Request for Evaluation**

A referral for a Section 504 evaluation may be initiated by a parent, guardian, teacher, counselor, administrator, or other school staff member who has reason to believe a student may have a disability requiring accommodations. Referrals shall be made in writing using the District Section 504 Referral Form (Form OAS-504-01) and submitted to the building's Section 504 Coordinator.

Upon receipt of a referral, the building Section 504 Coordinator shall:

- Acknowledge receipt of the referral in writing to the parent or guardian within five (5) school days.
- Convene a Section 504 Team to review the referral and determine whether an evaluation is warranted.
- Provide the parent or guardian with a copy of their procedural rights under Section 504, as outlined in the District's Notice of Parent and Student Rights.

The decision to conduct an evaluation shall be made by the Section 504 Team. If the team determines that an evaluation is not warranted, the parent or guardian shall be notified in writing of the decision and their procedural rights.

**4.4 Evaluation Process**

The Section 504 evaluation shall be conducted by qualified personnel and shall draw upon information from a variety of sources, including aptitude and achievement tests, teacher recommendations, physical condition, social or cultural background, and adaptive behavior. No single measure or assessment shall be used as the sole criterion for determining eligibility.

The evaluation shall be completed within sixty (60) calendar days of the receipt of the parent's or guardian's written consent for the evaluation, unless an extension is agreed upon in writing by the parent or guardian and the district.

documents.title: Office of Accessibility Services Procedural Manual 2024-2025
documents.content:
**5. Plan Development and Implementation**

**5.1 Development of the Section 504 Plan**

Upon determination of eligibility, the Section 504 Team shall develop a written Section 504 Plan for the student. The plan shall be developed within thirty (30) calendar days of the eligibility determination. The plan shall be individualized and based on the unique needs of the student, as identified through the evaluation process.

The Section 504 Plan shall include, at a minimum, the following components:

- A statement of the specific disability and the major life activity or activities substantially limited.
- A description of the accommodations, aids, services, and modifications to be provided.
- The name or position of the person responsible for implementing each accommodation.
- A statement of how the accommodations will be provided and monitored.
- The duration or review date of the plan.

The plan shall be developed by the Section 504 Team, which shall include the parent or guardian, the student when appropriate, and individuals knowledgeable about the student, the meaning of the evaluation data, and the placement options.

**5.2 Parental Consent and Agreement**

The District shall make reasonable efforts to obtain the informed consent of the parent or guardian prior to the initial implementation of the Section 504 Plan. If the parent or guardian does not consent to the plan, the District shall document the efforts made and may proceed with implementation if the plan is deemed necessary to provide a free appropriate public education (FAPE). The parent or guardian shall be provided with a copy of the plan and a Notice of Parent and Student Rights.

**5.3 Implementation of Accommodations**

Each building principal or designee shall be responsible for ensuring that the accommodations listed in a student's Section 504 Plan are implemented. Classroom teachers and other staff who work with the student shall be notified of the specific accommodations they are responsible for providing. Notification shall occur prior to the first day of the student's attendance in a class or activity, or as soon as practicable thereafter.

The building Section 504 Coordinator shall maintain a copy of each active Section 504 Plan and a log of staff notification. The log shall include the date of notification and the names of the staff notified.

**5.4 Monitoring of the Section 504 Plan**

The Section 504 Team shall monitor the implementation and effectiveness of each student's Section 504 Plan. Monitoring shall occur on an ongoing basis and shall include, at a minimum, the following activities:

- Review of student progress reports and grades.
- Consultation with teachers and other staff regarding the effectiveness of accommodations.
- Input from the parent or guardian.
- Observation of the student in the educational setting, as appropriate.

If the monitoring indicates that the plan is not effective, the Section 504 Coordinator shall convene the Section 504 Team to review and revise the plan.

**5.5 Annual Review**

Each Section 504 Plan shall be reviewed at least annually. The annual review shall be conducted by the Section 504 Team and shall include a discussion of the student's current needs, the effectiveness of the accommodations, and any changes that may be necessary.

The annual review shall be documented using the Section 504 Plan Review Form (Form OAS-504-04). The parent or guardian shall be invited to participate in the review and shall be provided with a copy of the completed review form.

**5.6 Reevaluation**

A reevaluation of a student's eligibility under Section 504 shall be conducted at least once every three (3) years, or more frequently if conditions warrant or if the parent or guardian or a teacher requests a reevaluation. A reevaluation shall also be conducted prior to a significant change in placement.

documents.title: Office of Accessibility Services Procedural Manual 2024-2025
documents.content:
**6.0 GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES FOR SECTION 504 AND ADA COMPLAINTS**

**6.1 Purpose**

The Office of Accessibility Services (OAS) shall provide a process for resolving complaints alleging discrimination on the basis of disability in programs, services, or activities operated by the District. This procedure is intended to provide a prompt and equitable resolution of complaints and shall be made available to students, parents, guardians, employees, and members of the public.

**6.2 Filing a Complaint**

Any individual who believes they have been subjected to discrimination on the basis of disability may file a complaint. Complaints shall be submitted in writing to the OAS Director or the District’s designated Section 504/ADA Coordinator. The complaint shall include the following information:

- The name and contact information of the complainant.
- The name of the student or individual affected, if different from the complainant.
- A description of the alleged discriminatory act or denial of accommodation.
- The date(s) on which the alleged act occurred.
- The name(s) of any District employee or program involved, if known.
- The specific remedy or resolution sought by the complainant.

Complaints shall be filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of the alleged discriminatory act, unless the complainant can demonstrate good cause for an extension. The OAS Director may waive the filing deadline upon a showing of extenuating circumstances.

**6.3 Investigation**

Upon receipt of a complaint, the OAS Director or a designee shall conduct an investigation. The investigation shall be completed within thirty (30) business days from the date the complaint is received. The investigator shall:

- Review all relevant records, including IEPs, Section 504 Plans, correspondence, and any other documentation related to the complaint.
- Interview the complainant, the student (if appropriate), relevant staff members, and any other witnesses identified during the investigation.
- Visit the location or observe the program or activity at issue, as appropriate.

The investigator shall prepare a written report of findings and submit the report to the OAS Director. The report shall include a determination of whether a violation of Section 504, the ADA, or District policy has occurred.

**6.4 Resolution and Notice**

Within ten (10) business days following the completion of the investigation, the OAS Director shall issue a written decision to the complainant. The decision shall include:

- A summary of the allegations.
- The findings of the investigation.
- A determination of whether a violation occurred.
- A description of any corrective action to be taken, if applicable.
- Notice of the right to appeal the decision.

Corrective action may include, but is not limited to, the provision of compensatory services, the modification of a student’s accommodation plan, staff training, or a change in District practice or procedure.

**6.5 Appeal**

The complainant may appeal the OAS Director’s decision by submitting a written notice of appeal to the Superintendent’s Office within fifteen (15) business days of the date of the decision. The appeal shall state the basis for the disagreement with the decision. The Superintendent or designee shall review the appeal and issue a final written decision within twenty (20) business days.

**6.6 Relationship to Other Procedures**

Nothing in this procedure shall prevent a complainant from pursuing other remedies available under federal, state, or local law, including filing a complaint with the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) or the U.S. Department of Justice. The District may coordinate its investigation with any external investigation, but shall not delay its own investigation solely because an external complaint has been filed.

Fall 2024 Accessibility Training Records
Office of Accessibility Services
Semester: Fall 2024
Report Date: 2024-12-20
Prepared by: Rita Okafor, Training Coordinator

This report covers the Fall 2024 training cycle for the Accessibility Fundamentals course (OAS-101) and the follow-up session on Assistive Technology Basics (OAS-102). All full-time staff in student-facing roles were required to complete OAS-101 by October 15, 2024. OAS-102 was offered as a recommended follow-up for departments with direct service responsibilities.

Summary of Completion Status

Total enrolled (OAS-101): 214
Completed: 206
Incomplete: 6
No-show: 2

Certificate numbers were issued upon completion of the course and the end-of-course quiz. Certificates are valid for two years from the date of completion. Staff who completed OAS-101 and then enrolled in OAS-102 are noted in the follow-up column below.
